claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is single-phase.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous microstructure and homogeneous distribution of constituent elements.
A suitable heat or thermomechanical treatment induces localized nanoscale ordering or clustering at grain boundaries.
The proposed grain-boundary ordering is distinct from simple solute segregation in conventional alloys.
A treatment window exists that promotes local ordering without macroscopic phase separation or grain coarsening.
Complex multi-element interactions drive the proposed local ordering process.
Ordered grain-boundary regions reduce local interfacial cohesion.
Ordered grain-boundary regions impede plastic deformation across the boundary.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion and impeded plastic transfer cause embrittlement despite retention of a macroscopically single-phase microstructure.
The treated alloy will have lower fracture toughness than the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will have lower ductility than the untreated baseline.
Nanoscale ordering or clustering at grain boundaries will correlate with the onset of brittle behavior.
The untreated homogeneous single-phase baseline exhibits a favorable strength-ductility combination and high toughness.
Maintaining similar grain size and overall composition between treated and untreated samples isolates the effect of localized grain-boundary ordering.
